findings.title: a supervisor that dies before receiving the key yields OK; the declared premature-termination -> TRANSFER_WRITE_FAILED arm is unreachable in practice
findings.mechanism: The governed key frame is 92 bytes and the inherited anonymous descriptor is an ordinary kernel pipe with a 64 KiB buffer. writer.write(frame, cb) therefore always completes into the buffer and writer.end()'s callback resolves done({ok:true}) within microseconds, long before the 250 ms timer that premature() arms on 'exit'/'close' can fire. Because done() is guarded by the `settled` flag, the premature arm's later done({code: TRANSFER_WRITE_FAILED}) is a no-op. The arm can therefore never decide an outcome that the writer 'error' arm would not already have decided, so 'child terminated before the key frame completed' is not a reachable result. The launcher returns ok:true with supervisor_pid set to a process that has already exited without ever reading fd 3.
findings.reproduction: Build a genuine disposable CONSUMED capability and a genuine ephemeral-signed launch intent whose supervisor entrypoint is a file containing exactly `process.exit(9);`. Call spawnGovernedSupervisorV4(cap, { detached: true }). Observed 6/6 times.
findings.actual_result: { ok: true, code: 'OK', transfer: 'TRANSFERRED_SPENT', supervisor_pid: <already-exited pid> }; no key receipt was written; the child's exit code is 9; a retry returns ALREADY_TRANSFERRED.
findings.required_result: a structured SUPERVISOR_SPAWN_FAILED or TRANSFER_WRITE_FAILED result, as the review contract requires for case 3 and as the correction ledger's own bullet states.
findings.spawn_count: 0 provider spawns; 1 disposable supervisor child, which exits on its own and leaves no residual process.
findings.security_impact: NONE to key containment. The authority is TRANSFERRED_SPENT, the private key is deleted from module storage before the first await, every temporary buffer is zeroed, the retry is refused ALREADY_TRANSFERRED, and the unread frame dies with the pipe when the kernel tears it down. The defect is EVIDENCE TRUTHFULNESS and LIVENESS: the launcher records a completed transfer and a live supervisor for a supervisor that provably never received the key, and a governing caller acting on that OK would wait for a claim that can never be minted.
findings.narrow_correction_scope: One of: (a) make the exit/close arm decisive on evidence rather than timing — at settle time, before returning OK, require child.exitCode === null && child.signalCode === null, or require a supervisor acknowledgement; or (b) if the timing heuristic is intentional, restate it truthfully in lifecycle-authority-v4.mjs:557-559 and in the ledger so no document claims a TRANSFER_WRITE_FAILED outcome the code does not produce. No change to the key-transfer, spend or retry semantics is needed — those are correct.

findings.title: deepFreezeAuthority silently drops an own __proto__ data key and mutates the copy's prototype instead of refusing it
findings.line: 85-91 (out = {}; out[k] = copyFreeze(d.value, ...) inside the getOwnPropertyNames loop)
findings.mechanism: `out` is created as {}, so it inherits Object.prototype's __proto__ accessor. When k === '__proto__', `out[k] = value` invokes that SETTER and reassigns the copy's prototype rather than creating an own data property. JSON.parse produces exactly this shape — an own, enumerable, writable __proto__ data property — so the one input class the module is built to consume can carry a key it neither refuses nor copies faithfully. The module's stated contract is that it 'accepts ONLY plain JSON authority data and refuses everything else rather than silently passing it through', and that a refusal throws rather than publishing a partially-formed structure; here it does neither.
findings.actual_result: no throw; Object.getOwnPropertyNames(f) === ['limits'] (the __proto__ key is gone); Object.getPrototypeOf(f) !== Object.prototype and is the attacker's object; f.max_budget_usd === 777777 and f.no_akior === false by prototype-chain lookup; Object.isFrozen(f) === true and mutableAuthorityPaths(f) === [] both still report the copy as sound; and the module REFUSES its own output on round-trip with AUTHORITY_NON_PLAIN_PROTOTYPE — a self-inconsistency proving the copy is not the plain-JSON authority data the contract promises.
findings.required_result: an own __proto__ key should raise AuthorityFreezeError (or be materialised with Object.defineProperty so the copy is faithful and the prototype stays Object.prototype).
findings.reachability: NOT CURRENTLY EXPLOITABLE, and this Checker verified it rather than assuming it. All three production call sites — activation-v4.mjs:137, lifecycle-authority-v4.mjs:230 and lifecycle-authority-v4.mjs:364 — pass object literals whose key sets are hard-coded in source, and cap.limits / cap.exclusions are built by Object.fromEntries over the fixed V4_SIGNED_LIMIT_FIELDS and V4_SIGNED_EXCLUSIONS tables. No attacker-controlled key reaches the helper on any route. This is a latent contract gap in an explicitly-audited helper, not an authority escape.
findings.narrow_correction_scope: One guard in copyFreeze: refuse (or defineProperty) the key '__proto__' in the object branch. Roughly one line plus a regression assertion; nothing else in the module or its call sites changes.
